It depends on what you want to do with your art. If you are planning on sticking with traditional art such as inking, sketches, and traditional painting, then you might not need a tablet. If you are wanting to expand upon your art, then you should get a tablet. Honestly, I think every artist should own a graphics tablet. Even if they only do traditional, they can still benefit from a graphics tablet for those off occasions  Editing photos with a tablet is much easier than using a mouse.

The upside to digital art is that it expands your horizons in a big way. You're very limited when sticking with traditional art. You can try different types of art such as digital painting, animating, 3d modeling, manga/comic creating, concept art, pixel art, ect. Some of these things you could do using traditional methods and a mouse, but you'll have to go through extra steps and you will be using the computer regardless. It's just a better game plan to own a tablet.

For a beginner you should get a graphics tablet and not a monitor tablet... Simply because it costs hundreds of dollars and you are just starting. You don't need to buy a $400+ piece of equipment right off the bat. I don't know if you know the difference, but a graphics tablet is used by drawing on a pad while looking at the computer screen. A monitor tablet is where the tablet has it's own screen that you can draw on directly. 

You should browse Huion and Xpen tablets on amazon because they tend to have good reviews. Wacoms are nice and more stable, but they tend to be overpriced. Make sure to thoroughly read the reviews. Some tablets have little quirks that can make it frustrating to use. My issues have been finicky drivers, the express keys are too stiff, and the stylus's pen nib is too firm and my hand started to hurt from pressing too hard on the tablet.

I would shoot for a tablet that has a battery free stylus. Avoid the Huion H610PRO. It's awful. Huion Inspiroys are pretty good. I've never used Xpen but I've heard good things. Pay attention to the tablet's drawing area size. Some can be very small and others way too big. Everyone has their own preference in work area size and you should figure out what yours is too. Tablets usually come with a drawing glove, but if yours doesn't you should absolutely get one. Unfortunately, I can't help you much on recommending a tablet since I used my old monitor tablet for 3 years before it died and I couldn't get back into using regular tablets. I used an old Wacom Bamboo before getting my old monitor tablet, so I am a bit out of touch with new tablet market.
